speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Liang, Ms Tan, Mr Chia and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked if the Government could make it easier for startups and businesses with innovative solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They highlighted that heavy administrative burdens and the expectations of having a track record might hamper their access to government procurement opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Today, many agencies require businesses to demonstrate track record and financial capacity so that only businesses able to deliver the projects are selected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This helps to ensure reliability, especially for goods, services and infrastructure used by the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But it can be challenging if the proposed solution is new to the market, especially a new technology or product, and more so if the business is a startup.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Further, the pilot phase and the deployment phase are typically structured as separate tenders today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: A business that wins the tender for the pilot phase has no certainty that it will get to deploy its solution at scale with the Government, even if the pilot was successful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This means that businesses can be assured of the opportunity to scale up its innovative product or service, if the pilot is successful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: More details will be provided in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Last year, we said that the Government would improve the promptness of payments to vendors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Liang asked what measures the Government is taking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We have worked with SBF and ASME to survey businesses to better understand the current process gaps.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Today, almost all the invoices billed to Government agencies adopt 30 days or shorter credit terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We remain committed to keep prompt payment rates above 95%.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Furthermore, MOF will provide Government agencies with guidelines to address businesses' suggestions that include having more payment milestones and clarifying administrative processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The issue of prompt payment is one that extends beyond government procurement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: SBF is setting up a workgroup to review the development of a Code for transactions between businesses and we welcome this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Liang and Mr Chia asked what MOF agencies are doing to improve the experience of transacting with Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This has been a continuous endeavour for MOF agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Today, it is relatively easy to file taxes with IRAS and apply for customs permits with Customs, following many years of system enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But improvements can always be made, and we will continue to make them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Since November 2024, IRAS has expedited tax clearance for employers filing on behalf of non-citizen employees who cease employment in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Previously, employers would typically need to wait two to three days to receive IRAS' Directive to pay tax and release monies to the employee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: IRAS now issues the Directive on the same day for straightforward cases, which make up 70% of filings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This will apply to about 180,000 filings a year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Customs has been exploring the use of AI to address a pain point for traders today – finding the right product codes and licenses applicable to their products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: There is a search engine today, but it requires traders to use specific technical search terms to retrieve the correct codes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Customs has been working with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, the Government Technology Agency and the Public Service Division to develop a new search engine using AI.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: It will allow traders to search for the right product codes using layman descriptions and it will also make recommendations on the required licenses for controlled goods, as a further value-add.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The new search engine will be more user-friendly and help traders navigate the regulatory landscape more efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The new search engine will be soft launched later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Following the soft launch, agencies will gather public feedback and make necessary refinements to the search engine.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: From next month, Customs will also progressively implement new data analytics tools to better service public enquiries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This tool will allow Customs to leverage real-time data insights to identify patterns in enquiries raised on customs procedures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Chairman, my colleagues and I have laid out what MOF will do to: (a) enhance our pro-enterprise environment and make Government a better partner to businesses; (b) ensure responsible and effective governance of our public resources today and tomorrow; and (c) prepare Singapore for long-term challenges on the climate and to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Let us continue to work together to keep Singapore forward-looking, united and confident.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My question is directed to Minister Indranee vis-a-vis my cut.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If I heard the Minister correctly, the Minister said, land for HDB developments is typically priced lower than that for private housing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I confirm how is the differential then determined by the CV between private housing and land for HDB?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think, what Mr Singh is asking is "what is the methodology or the workings of the CV?" I am not privy to the workings of the CV.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What I can say is the principles that she applies, which is the principles that I had elucidated earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I mean, it is just like when you have an MRT track.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If you ask the engineer to design the rail track or you ask an architect to build something, you do not go and ask them for all of their internal drawings and so on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Valuation, as everybody knows, is part science, part art.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You need some experience, you need to make relevant adjustments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And this is the same whether it is the CV or whether it is valuers in the private sector.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in short, what I have explained is the principles that she would apply and from site to site, it may differ, depending on locational attributes and particular characteristics of the site.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: I appreciate that the Government provides a lot of support for training.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Nonetheless, Government is actually a very big buyer of creator services.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: This is very much like career trials, where we give people opportunities to practise and then, of course, to build their portfolios so that they can move on to bigger opportunities.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: In fact, our NTUC's Visual, Audio, Creative Content Professionals Association, we actually stand ready to support the Government if there is interest to do something like that.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I wish to clarify with the Minister that I did not make a general statement about productivity and wages in my cut.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: But when I mentioned productivity, that was specific to my seeking clarification from the Minister about whether there has been any analysis done about what effects the programme has had on employers investing in productivity improvements beyond skills upgrading.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: There was no contradiction with my colleague's Budget intervention on this, as he said that wages need to catch up with productivity gains that have already occurred.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: On this point, can the Minister share if this analysis has been done?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: My concern here is that the uncertainty about whether the scheme will be extended will make businesses currently on the scheme more cautious and less keen to take action to either invest in or increase wages now and will delay any such decisions until they hear the next announcement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I think the Prime Minister had already explained in his round-up speech about how productivity and wages, over time, do move in tandem.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And on that point, the Prime Minister had already explained very thoroughly and I would not repeat.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I just wanted to go back to my response to Ms He earlier that we do not disagree that we need to look at how to improve productivity of firms.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why we do have many schemes in place to help our companies, whether is it SMEs or larger companies, or as Mr Neil Parekh suggested, how do we encourage more SMEs to work closely with the larger companies, whether it is a large local enterprise or a multinational enterprise.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it is not a broad-based subsidy, as I explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But it is for the Government to co-share some of the cost increases that employers would otherwise have to face when they are trying to help their low-wage workers to earn a higher salary.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope this is in line with what Ms He said.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I said earlier in my main reply to her that I am sure she is not suggesting that we should not support SMEs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is difficult to say we will end it if the following boxes are checked because we have to look at the situation at that time.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There are a lot of uncertainties in our operating environment globally and the challenges that our companies will face; it is something which we do need to consult with our tripartite partners before making that decision.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I also do not fully agree, Mr Chairman, with Ms He's framing that just because we are providing this support for our SMEs, to help them to co-fund, not fully fund, but to co-fund some of the cost increases for low-wage workers earning a higher income, that they will then not want to improve productivity.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not think that is the way the businesses would respond to the various schemes and incentives.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think he prepared some comments with regard to the disclosure of the size of the reserve and assets under management.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But in my speech, I specifically mentioned that actually, that was not what I was talking about.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: It is more about the performance figures where you have Temasek disclosing annual figures and MAS disclosing annual figures.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Why is it that GIC cannot do so?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Second, specific to Minister Indranee's point about the CDC Vouchers, I take her point that, yes, the cost of living hits everyone.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But the point that I was trying to make is that it does not hit everyone the same, which is why, if you look at the $800 worth of vouchers, to a lower-income household versus a high-income household, it is a very different percentage of their expenditure.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: That is why in my gist and also in my main Budget speech yesterday, what I was saying is that we need to have a more targeted approach.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: An example which I have given in delivering the cut was to maybe leverage on the CHAS card scheme, because you already have the Blue CHAS card holders, Orange and Green.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The different income groups, is quite nicely partitioned that way.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, that is something that we can leverage on.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The question then is, would the Minister not agree that this is more in line with how the Government generally directs assistance packages?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is just to respond to Mr Chua's question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Chua for his clarification.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is perhaps not that much difference really in what we are looking at.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chua's point is that different people have different incomes, so you should give more to those who have less.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that is the point, and that has consistently been the Government's position.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not understand Mr Chua to be saying, do not give the others anything, right?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that too, is common ground, because Mr Chua is not saying, "do not give the middle-income" and "do not give the higher-income".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, we give retirees Silver Support over and above right.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, even for the U-Save utilities, the rental flats get more.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you can see that we have a slew of programmes which are targeted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But at the same time, everybody is feeling the pain of cost of living.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Dennis Tan spoke about it in the Cost-of-living Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Yesterday, Mr Faisal Manap talked about the middle-income.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, in clarification, the Leader of the Opposition also highlighted middle-income.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And even the higher-income is saying they feel that things are more expensive.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it is necessary to also have something for everyone, because we empathise with how they feel.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But because the pain on the ground at that time was quite a lot, we wanted to help everybody and hence, CDC Vouchers were made universal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that does not take away from the fact that we have targeted schemes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And it also does not preclude the fact that perhaps for CHAS, we can also leverage that to see how we can triangulate better.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: It is not to say that I do not support businesses.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: It is just that the concerns that I raised in my cut were systemic to the long-term effects for what was initially meant to be a temporary scheme.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms He for her clarification.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think we are on the same page.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The approach that we want to take, whether on this scheme or on many other schemes, is that when we want to do something that will be good for Singapore and Singaporeans, we want to do it together with our stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is also in line, I think, with the spirit of Forward SG.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I believe all the clarifications have been raised and answered.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And also, I want to thank Prime Minister Wong and the best-in-class MOF team for yet another impactful Budget that stands us in good stead to move Singapore forward.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
